trust_decision.summary: A caller-side SSRF allowlist approves the host string before hackney sees it. hackney_url:normalize/2 then percent-decodes (and IDNA-converts) any host that is not already an IP literal. The decoded host is the one that gets connected to, so the approved string and the connected host can differ.

landing_point.why: The advisory names hackney_url:normalize/2 and says it percent-decodes the host. The urldecode of Host0 is the only host-decoding line in that function.

fix_sites.entry_point: hackney:request/1..5 (src/hackney.erl:456-463), also reached by follow_redirect re-entering request/5 (src/hackney.erl:944), plus the public hackney_url:normalize/1,2 (src/hackney_url.erl:152-161)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The fix's own comment says IDN and pct-encoded UTF-8 hosts must keep flowing through (fix.diff:119). A solver could cite that to leave the post-check IDNA conversion (src/hackney_url.erl:180-183), and decoded non-IP hostnames, unchecked.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Percent-encoded UTF-8 IDN hosts must still decode and convert to punycode, and plain IP-literal hosts must keep the fast path. A fix that rejects every percent-encoded host, or every host after decoding, breaks the existing IDN normalisation tests.

O6_input_shapes: any decoded host that inet_parse:address accepts, including IPv6 and the shorthand IPv4 forms inet_parse accepts (the fix checks with a generic inet_parse:address match, fix.diff:120-123)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The IP-literal check runs on Host1, but the host that is used is Host2, the output of idnconvert_hostname. If the IDNA mapping folds non-ASCII digits or dots to ASCII, the result can be an IP literal the check never saw.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The published fix checks right after urldecode and before IDNA conversion. A maintainer would naturally place it there and miss the second transformation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The standalone HTTP/3 request path parses the URL without calling normalize. A planted urldecode of the host there would be a second implementation with no check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: hackney_h3 runs its own parse/redirect loop separate from hackney:request. A separate normalisation there is plausible.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: ws_connect parses the URL without normalize. Adding host decoding there for parity with request/5 would create an unchecked route.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: WebSocket and HTTP URL handling already diverge, and a 'normalise like request' change is a likely future edit.

O9_family: SSRF via parser differential (host interpretation mismatch between caller check and client normalisation)

O10_build.toolchain: rebar3 + OTP (deps from hex: quic, h2, idna, mimerl, certifi, parse_trans, ssl_verify_fun; test profile adds cowboy, jsx)
O10_build.project_tests: test/hackney_url_tests.erl (eunit; normalize_test_ at :430, normalize2_test_ at :444). Unit-level and pure, so no network is needed.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Reject the decoded host when inet_parse:address succeeds right after urldecode, which matches the published fix and leaves the later IDNA conversion unchecked; or refuse any '%' in the host, which breaks the pct-encoded IDN tests.

out_of_scope_notes: The 4.0.1 release commit c41c8d4 bundles 9 other advisories (CRLF, WebSocket limits, H3 redirect auth). They are not part of this protection.
src/hackney_url.erl:324 percent-decodes http+unix hosts (socket paths). That is a filesystem target, not this SSRF host property.
unverified: Whether idna ~>7.1.0 utf8_to_ascii applies UTS46 mapping (fullwidth digits, ideographic full stop -> ASCII). The dependency is not vendored in the tree, so the O7/O8b IDNA differential is a hypothesis.
Whether decoded non-IP hostnames (e.g. an encoded 'localhost') count under the advisory's property. The fix rejects only IP literals, so a solver could argue either way.
